entities.summary: Dick Higgins was an American artist, composer, art theorist, poet, publisher, printmaker, and a co-founder of the Fluxus international artistic movement. Inspired by John Cage, Higgins was an early pioneer of electronic correspondence. Higgins coined the word intermedia to describe his artistic activities, defining it in a 1965 essay by the same name, published in the first number of the Something Else Newsletter. His most notable audio contributions include Danger Music scores and the Intermedia concept to describe the ineffable inter-disciplinary activities that became prevalent in the 1960s.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a co-founder of Fluxus and pioneer of electronic correspondence, Dick Higgins played a significant role in shaping the development of intermedia art in the 1960s, influencing artists such as John Cage and conceptualizing the concept of intermedia that became prevalent during this era.
